html:<span class=\"tag c\">连接组</span><b>: html:connectomeKnock out real neurons: this row of switches are real neurons picked by the virtual knockout screen (report §14–24, 24,250 whole-brain simulation segments), not functional groups. Cutting their outgoing synapses uses the same semantics as the whole-brain screen. The two numbers on each switch are the same neuron's ratio in the sugar pathway and in the water pathway, measured in this sub-circuit (node dodge/measure_neurons.js: pellet pinned 1.3 mm in front of the head in continuous contact → taste neurons at 200 Hz, 3 seeds, mean over the last 1.25 s of 2.5 s); hover to see the whole-brain value (python dodge/measure_neurons_fullbrain.py, 138,639 neurons, same joint knockout + null-median normalization + 6 realizations). But it must be said clearly: this sub-circuit has only 4,599 neurons (3% of the whole brain), so individual neurons can be noticeably distorted. The biggest difference is CB0883—in the whole brain it is a hub ("0.76 knocked out alone, collapsing to 0.24 only when paired with Clavicle/G2N-1"), but in the sub-circuit it has no effect at all (sugar ×1.07, water ×1.00), and pairing is merely additive, because the bypass routes it depends on were cut during pruning. Conversely, Clavicle + G2N-1 is still synergistic in the sub-circuit (0.91 / 0.67 each, 0.50 together, 0.61 expected if independent). Most worth looking at is the contrast between sugar and water: Clavicle barely affects sugar (×0.91) but zeroes water (×0.01); CB0051 likewise (×0.80 / ×0.02); G2N-1 conversely only matters for sugar (×0.67 / ×1.07); Phantom is inhibitory, and knocking it out actually doubles MN9 in the water pathway (×2.06). This is what the conclusion of report §21 looks like in the game—the same proboscis extension, driven by two different sets of wiring. Comparing these 10 neurons' ratios in the whole brain and the sub-circuit as a whole [exploratory, n = 10]: sugar Pearson +0.75, water +0.89—overall the sub-circuit reproduces the whole-brain knockout pattern, somewhat more closely on the water side. The most striking row is still Phantom: knock it out and whole-brain water-pathway MN9 becomes 3.02×, sub-circuit 2.06×—direction and magnitude both match. (This cell previously said "sugar +0.21, water +0.92, the sub-circuit reproduces only the water pathway", which was wrong: sugar used un-normalized values and only the 6 named types; with a unified protocol and all 10 neurons, sugar rises to +0.75.)
html:第一个标签默认进的就是它（「世界」开关可以切回篮球场）。地形、石头、蘑: html:The first tab opens straight into it (the "World" switch can take you back to the court). Terrain, stones, mushrooms, flowers, grass, berry bushes and puddles are all generated deterministically from a seed, and the game core and the 3D renderer use the same world object—the stone you see drawn is the stone it bumps into. Physics uses real units: gravity 9,810 mm/s²; berries fall from branches, bounce along the terrain normal, roll downhill and ferment once they settle; stones are impenetrable; walking uphill is slower; the sun heats dark slabs; hollows fill with rain and evaporate in sunshine; wind carries scent downwind. The fly knows all of this only through real receptors (slope → walking speed, solid objects → blocked path + antennae pressed, slabs → temperature receptors, rain → humidity receptors and auditory neurons, fermenting berries → olfactory sensory neurons, beetles and falling berries → looming vision), and not a single new behaviour rule was added. The threat changed from "flying balls" to "crawling beetles": at the millimetre scale, a 60 mm/s projectile hits the ground in 0.1 s and stops after rolling a few millimetres, so a ball slowly rolling towards you is not physical.

html:<b>两处按数据改过设计，值得写出来</b>：①「一个不够，两个才行」: html:Two designs were changed based on data, and they are worth writing down: ① "One isn't enough, it takes two" originally drew the line at 8 s, and a single knockout could pass too; measured per run—no intervention 6.1/8.6/11.2 s, Clavicle alone 5.4/8.1/5.1, G2N-1 alone 4.8/6.8/7.9, both together 2.8/2.9/2.0—so the line moved to 4 s, between "the lowest single knockout, 4.8" and "the highest double knockout, 2.9". ② "Prove the connectome really matters" originally judged the dodge rate, but after shuffling the per-run values were 0.07/0.79/0.43—so variable that one run was about the same as unshuffled, so the criterion was switched to the number of takeoffs (shuffled 18/5/0 vs no intervention 33/32/33, no overlap at all), which is also closer to the mechanism: what shuffling breaks first is the looming → giant fibre route.
html:几点必须说明：<b>苦味「没有落点」是对的</b>——它是抑制性的，单: html:A few things must be explained: it is correct that bitter "has no landing point"—it is inhibitory, so on its own it should not drive anything; its role is to suppress sugar-driven MN9 (paper Fig 3B–C, which we reproduced: under the strongest sugar, bitter suppresses 82.4%). Humidity genuinely has no landing point—no strength of drive moves any motor output. Temperature only has one above 400 Hz, which at reasonable stimulus strengths means none. Touch has one at 100–200 Hz, which is why it lets the fly get around the fence. One more interesting point: touch given to both sides at once is actually weaker (at 200 Hz all six readouts are 0)—symmetric left-right drive cancels the left-right difference that steering needs. This is not a bug; it is how the circuit is.
html:But simply averaging many frames does not help—measured improvement −0.2%, because each measurement is itself a blurred average over ommatidia, and stacking them just averages more blurred images. What actually works is back-projection: solve an inverse problem to find a high-resolution image such that "measuring it with the ommatidia" reproduces all 69,216 measurements. Measured correlation with the original: single frame 0.851 → naive accumulation 0.849 → back-projection 0.920, exceeding the ceiling of 0.883 set by a single acceptance angle —— showing it really recovers information from multiple frames that a single frame does not contain. It uses only measured values and known geometry, with no statistics from training data, unlike the decoders in the four columns on the right.
html:<b>v1 的全部数字作废。</b>这张卡片以前写的是「果蝇脑的一致率: html:All v1 numbers are void. This card used to say "the fly brain's agreement rate is 0.025, only slightly above chance; the connectome contributes nothing to playing". That version had a bug: when the brain's input was changed, the previous batch of stimulation was not cleared, so inputs piled up one after another. As a result almost every board fed in was the same input, and the readout learned noise. The other half of the cause was architecture: v1 spread the whole board randomly over sensory neurons, discarding the locality and translation invariance that matter most in Gomoku. The game itself is not affected by this bug (every step rewrites the whole input group; the results of 7 missions and 10 mutants are identical item by item before and after the fix).
html:<b>看不出来的那三个才是重点</b>：G2N-1、Zorro、CB0: html:The three you cannot tell apart are the point: after knocking out G2N-1, Zorro or CB0883, all six behavioural measures fall within the normal range. This is not a flaw in the game—it is the behavioural version of the conclusion the whole-brain screen kept reaching: a single knockout often shows nothing. CB0883 is a hub in the whole brain (0.76 knocked out alone, collapsing to 0.24 when paired with Clavicle/G2N-1), and Zorro is a type real experiments confirmed as "required for proboscis extension", yet when either is knocked out alone the fly looks perfectly normal. To find them, you must knock them out in pairs—which is exactly the "One isn't enough, it takes two" mission.
html:七个手术任务，玩家只准动开关（断突触 / 敲真实神经元 / 打乱接线: html:Seven surgery missions; the player may only touch the switches (cut synapses / knock out real neurons / shuffle wiring / optogenetic pulses), not change the rules. The question is: how do you know a mission is designed correctly? Our approach is to run each mission twice with node dodge/mission_test.js—no intervention and reference solution, 3 seeds × 60 s each—and then set the pass line from the measured distribution. If a mission can be passed without intervention, it tests nothing; if the reference solution cannot pass, the mission is impossible. The table below gives all measured values.

html:<b>一篇值得读的批评</b>：Patrick Mineault，<i: html:A critique worth reading: Patrick Mineault, Deconstructing viral fly sims (2026-09-14, neuroai.science). His core objection: most demos do not build a complete sensory-to-motor closed loop, and visual input acts roughly like a random seed; and "a large enough network can learn many things anyway—does it matter that it is a fly?". The strict standard he proposes: behaviour must be genuinely driven by the senses, activity must be electrophysiologically plausible, and it must show individuality.
html:<b>如实说明：</b>默认的视觉前端仍是手写的逼近检测，石头、草、地: html:Honestly: the default visual front end is still the hand-written looming detector, and stones, grass and terrain are not in its vision—it gets around stones by sliding along them after being blocked, plus antennal touch. The real pixel path "Dodge by eyes only" in the compound-eye window is now also wired to this fly, but once it walks, the grass everywhere becomes false looming, so it is off by default. The fly's own body is kinematic and does not fall over; berries are what gravity acts on. Puddles are a water level, not a fluid. Terrain amplitude, object density, the restitution coefficient 0.35, rolling resistance 0.15, the slope coefficient and the weather rhythm are all hand-picked.
html:一个没有边界的 3D 大自然：起伏的地形、石头、蘑菇、花、浆果丛、水洼: html:A boundless 3D Nature: rolling terrain, stones, mushrooms, flowers, berry bushes, puddles, day and night, wind and rain, with gravity—ripe berries fall, bounce a few times, roll downhill and ferment once they settle; stones block the way; walking uphill is slower; the sun heats slabs; wind carries scent downwind; beetles crawl towards you. The fly knows this world only through real receptors; which way to turn, whether to fly, whether to eat are decided by this connectome of 15,055 neurons—there is no rule like "run when you see a beetle" or "go over when you smell fruit".
html:报告里有一份<strong>错误账本</strong>，记录所有自己发: html:The report contains an error ledger recording every error we found and fixed ourselves, never deleted. Three rounds of number-by-number checking found 48 problems, including: the simulation software compiled the random seed into the program, so "4 runs" were actually 4 copies of one run; an accuracy of "2/2" in a table was a hand-written string, and one of its neurons was never tested; and right after writing "agreement rate is misleading, look at κ", the κ we quoted ourselves was filled in wrong twice.
html:<span class=\"tag h\">手写 · 非连接组</sp: html:hand-written · not connectome"Follow the scent" (off by default): pellets emit a Gaussian scent field (σ = 15 mm); the left and right antennae each sample the concentration, and when concentration > 0.01 the fly turns towards the higher side at 120°/s, added on top of DNa steering; pellets already tasted no longer attract. In the whole-brain model a one-sided odour stimulus gives no steering signal, so this step is entirely hand-written; whether it eats after touching a pellet is still decided by the connectome's sugar/bitter → MN9.
html:13 万个神经元、1,500 万条突触——一只果蝇大脑的完整接线图，在: html:130,000 neurons, 15 million synapses—the complete wiring diagram of a fruit-fly brain was mapped and open-sourced in 2024. This project runs it on a 16 GB MacBook, connects it to a physical body, turns it into a game playable in the browser, and has performed 18,799 virtual surgeries on it. This page records what it can do, what it cannot do, and every error the author found on self-review.
html:上传一张图，果蝇用它<b>真实的视觉系统</b>看一遍，再画出来。链路: html:Upload an image, and the fly looks at it with its real visual system and then draws it back. There are no schematic shortcuts in the pipeline: your image first becomes a 450×512 camera frame, is pooled into 721 ommatidia using FlyGym's real compound-eye sampling table (including fisheye distortion), then fed into flyvis's pretrained connectome visual network (65 cell types × 721 columns, 2355 convolution taps), and finally reconstructed by a hexagonal-convolution decoder.
html:<b>那就只给它物理量，让它自己决定。</b>这是最干净的做法，我们试: html:Then give it only physical quantities and let it decide. That is the cleanest approach, and we tried it: antennae touching the fence → drive mechanosensory neurons. The result: the fly did not react at all (the wall-hugging rate did not move by a single percentage point). The reason is in the connectome: the only mechanosensation in the game's sub-circuit is the antennal JO, and JO connects only to the grooming command aDN1, not to steering or escape at all.
html:还有一处是我们自己的指标错误，值得写出来：第一版用「贴墙时间占比」当指: html:There was also an error in our own metric, worth writing down: the first version used "fraction of time against the wall" as the metric, and it cannot tell "pinned at one spot" from "sliding along the wall"—the flag is true in both cases. By that metric touch was "useless" (85.6% → 85.6%); only after switching to the number of grid cells visited did it become clear that the fly had in fact been moving along the wall all along. Pick the wrong metric and the negative result is fake.

The table below is all the results, including what we could not do and what came out negative—both are results too. Each one traces to the script and result file that produced it; the complete lab notebook is docs/log/report.md in the repository.
html:果蝇会<b>扫视</b>，原因有两个，都不是为了好看。其一，T4/T5: html:The fly saccades, for two reasons, neither of them cosmetic. First, T4/T5 are motion detectors and barely respond to a static image. Second: neighbouring ommatidia are 16.4 pixels apart, so without moving it would always sample the same set of points—a 721-tile mosaic; once it moves, the same ommatidium lands on different places in the world (real flies do this too; it is called microsaccadic hyperacuity).
html:<b>后四栏是解码重建，会「补」出神经活动里其实没有的细节</b>——: html:The last four columns are decoded reconstructions and will "fill in" detail that is not actually in the neural activity—the decoder learns the statistics of the training images. The third column is the raw, undecoded activity, and the gap between the two is itself the thing to look at (same as the §15 decoder stress test). The further right the layer, the more of the image is lost: by T4/T5 only large shapes remain and fine stripes are gone.
